answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with live confluence sessions: each epoch, identities are randomly grouped into small crews that must jointly finish a fresh task in one short window, each signing a distinct piece the others build on, like a river crew rowing against the tide. One operator cannot staff thousands of crews at once, and copied work fails because every quill stroke is fresh and interdependent. A farm must pay a live worker per fake crew, while one honest agent rows once.
